title: WMI evaluation outcomes, loopback modes, and slow-link registry behavior
blocked_reason: Two of its three claims are now verified, by lane scenarios rather than by this file: loopback merge and replace certified 2026-08-04 (WP-9, loopback-merge and loopback-replace), and WMI true/false certified the same day (WP-6B, wmi-filtering, as the declared divergence WI-035). What keeps this scenario blocked is the SLOW-LINK half alone, and for two independent reasons: the estate cannot produce a genuinely slow link -- Group Policy measures bandwidth across the private switch and finds it fast -- and rsop.py does not read its own slow_link field anyway (WI-036), so there is currently nothing on either side to compare.

provenance.note: WMI-true applies and WMI-false filters are documented; the evaluation-error outcome is a recorded hypothesis (treated as false) that must be captured, not assumed. Loopback merge semantics (computer-location user settings win conflicts) are documented and are also a named Plan 033 precondition: Studio's earlier merge order was wrong. Slow-link: the registry CSE always processes; other CSE behaviors are outside Studio's model and recorded as open questions.

operator_meaning: Three WMI filters whose truth values are known by construction: true, false, and evaluation error
A user setting authored in a GPO linked at the computer's location, so loopback decides the winner against the user's own location GPO
Slow link toggled for the registry CSE, which always processes

denied.reason: WMI filter evaluation error treated as false (hypothesis to capture)

winners.reason: loopback disabled: normal user precedence, the computer-location GPO's user settings do not apply
loopback merge: computer-location user settings apply after and win conflicts (the Plan 033 precondition Studio previously got backwards)
loopback replace: only computer-location user settings apply
replace discards the user's own location GPOs entirely
the registry CSE always processes, including over slow links

derivations: Every mode is a separate gpupdate/gpresult cycle on the snapshot-backed client; loopback mode is set on the computer-location GPO (Studio-RSOP-ComputerLoc) per Windows convention.
Studio's compute_rsop exposes simulate_slow_link and loopback modes; the scenario binds each mode to the exact expected winner set so a precedence regression is a one-line diff.
The WMI error case is a recorded hypothesis (filtered out) until the first capture; if Windows applies the GPO on error, this file and Studio's model change together.

open_questions: Does a WMI evaluation error filter the GPO out (the hypothesis) or let it apply, and what reason does gpresult report?
Does the slow-link detection threshold on the qualified client need harness control (forced flag) or is a naturally metered link required for honest evidence?
